significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that multilingual factual disagreement decomposes into "a language-agnostic instability" plus a language-specific residual, that "only the residual scales with script/typological distance," and that the two components depend causally on mid-layer concept computation versus a late-layer transition; this combines a form-(iii) measurable relation with a form-(ii) causal decomposition. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, fixing expected distance correlations, the interpretation of cross-lingual error rates, and which processing stage explains each of two distinct failure classes; mLAMA (Kassner et al., 2021) and ParaRel (Elazar et al., 2021) illustrate that multilingual retrieval and paraphrase sensitivity are load-bearing evaluation axes whose attribution affects factual-knowledge conclusions. The branches are determinate and informative: a small baseline would rule out paraphrase instability as a major confound, while equal distance scaling or shared causal loci would reject the claimed separation rather than merely report non-detection. Topic-substitution check: deleting this additive decomposition, differential scaling law, and two-stage causal account leaves only the generic shared-versus-language-specific topic, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is the explicitly defined "language-specific residual"—cross-lingual disagreement "minus the pooled within-language baseline"—along with separate baseline and residual rates that audits can report. It is post hoc with respect to each benchmark answer but ex ante with respect to deployment because the claim specifically targets "model-release consistency claims" and "factuality/safety audits," giving evaluators an opportunity to screen or gate a model before shipping. After per-model re-estimation, the conclusion predicts a relation rather than merely supplying a search procedure: the residual, but not the paraphrase baseline, should scale with script or typological distance, although its asserted scope remains multilingual factual QA rather than reasoning generally or modalities outside language. Topic-substitution check: the generic multilingual-representation topic supplies neither this corrected metric nor its release-audit use, so the reach score comes from claim-specific handles available to benchmark designers and model auditors.
